## 1. Fixed question, dedup and scope

The local freeze is
CM24_ORDINARY_LEGENDRE_FROBENIUS_COMPARISON_LOCAL_FREEZE_20261015.json.

    P(s)=K_0(s)=P_n(s),  P(1)=1,
    L_n P=0,
    L_n=(1-s²)D²−2sD+lambda, lambda=n(n+1).              (1)

P is the exact polynomial over Z_(p), not its reduction substituted into
a new family. Its degree is n and it is even. These are saved inputs.

Put

    B=Z_(p)[s,(1-s²)^(-1)],
    C=Z_(p)[s,(1-s²)^(-1),(1-s^(2p))^(-1)],
    A(s)=[[0,1],[-lambda/(1-s²),2s/(1-s²)]].            (2)

The basepoint s=0 is ordinary. There are TWO maps B→C: iota(s)=s and
phi(s)=s^p, both identity on Z_(p). Modulo p, phi is the Frobenius map

    F(0)=diag(1,p),

## 2. A finite integral rational frame, with every denominator

There is a unique ODD polynomial U_n of degree≤n−1 satisfying

    L_n U_n=2P'.                                       (4)

This is a constructive finite assertion. Write P=sum a_j s^j and
U_n=sum_(j odd,1≤j≤n−1) u_j s^j. Descending through those j, set
u_(n+1)=0 and

    u_j=[2(j+1)a_(j+1)−(j+2)(j+1)u_(j+2)]
                               /[(n−j)(n+j+1)].       (5)

Both factors of every denominator are positive and below p:
1≤n−j≤n and n+j+1≤2n<p. Thus all are p-units. The diagonal factors
are nonzero over Q as well. Formula(5) proves existence, uniqueness
and U_n∈Z_(p)[s]; no prime example or linear solver is involved.
This is an auxiliary companion frame, not the old T construction or
an expansion of the killed four-column class.

Use the characteristic-zero FORMAL series

    ell(s)=sum_(j≥1 odd) s^j/j,  ell(0)=0,
    ell'(s)=1/(1-s²).                                 (6)

No analytic integral or evaluation of this series at an arithmetic unit
is used. ell itself is NOT p-integral. Define Q=P*ell−U_n. The product
rule and(1),(4) give L_n(P*ell)=2P', hence L_n Q=0. Introduce

    G(s)=[[P, −U_n],
          [P', P/(1-s²)−U_n']],  N=[[0,1],[0,0]].       (7)

The matrix with columns (P,P') and (Q,Q') is G(s)(I+ell(s)N).
Its Wronskian is

    d(s)=det G=P²/(1-s²)−P U_n'+P' U_n.

The homogeneous equation for P,Q gives
`d'=2s*d/(1-s²)`, so (1-s²)d is constant. Its explicit polynomial
expression evaluated at s=1 equals P(1)²=1. Therefore

    det G=1/(1-s²),
    G'=A G−G*N/(1-s²).                                (8)

The second identity also follows by checking its two columns using(4).
G is in GL_2(B). For clarity its inverse is polynomial:

    G^(-1)=[[P−(1-s²)U_n', (1-s²)U_n],
            [−(1-s²)P', (1-s²)P]].                    (9)

At0, P'=U_n=0 by parity, and(8) shows

    G(0)=diag(P(0),P(0)^(-1)), P(0) a p-unit.           (10)

The unit claim follows inside Z_(p) from the product of its two
diagonal entries being1, without a new sample or endpoint fit.

## 3. The p-scaled horizontal matrix is integral

Define, first as characteristic-zero formal series,

    b_p(s)=p*ell(s)−ell(s^p),
    H_p(s)=[[1,b_p(s)],[0,p]],
    F(s)=G(s)H_p(s)G(s^p)^(-1).                        (11)

For an odd exponent j divisible by p, the two coefficients in b_p
cancel EXACTLY: p/j−1/(j/p)=0. Every remaining coefficient equals
p/j with p not dividing j. Consequently

    b_p(s)=p*sum_(j≥1 odd,p∤j) s^j/j
          ∈p Z_(p)[[s]].                              (12)

This proves full formal p-integrality, not just a bounded truncation.
It explicitly handles all resonant exponents rather than discarding
the derivative kernel. G and G(s^p)^(-1) are integral at0, so F has
coefficients in Z_(p)[[s]].

In the logarithmic frame,

    H_p'=N*ell'(s)*H_p−p*s^(p−1)*H_p*N*ell'(s^p),      (13)

because NH_p=pN and H_p N=N. Equations(8),(13) prove the complete
horizontal equation(3), with both pullback terms. Equation(10) commutes
with diag(1,p), so F(0)=diag(1,p) as prescribed. In characteristic
zero an ordinary-point matrix ODE has a unique formal solution for
its full initial matrix, by its coefficient recursion. That is the
uniqueness intended here; arbitrary solutions specified only modulo
p² need not be unique from a point value.

The determinant is

    det F=p*(1-s^(2p))/(1-s²).                         (14)

Thus F is deliberately NONUNIT integrally, with a p times unit
determinant on C. Before finite-precision reduction the formal matrix
becomes invertible after extending scalars to Q. This is an explicit
isogeny-type comparison, not an integral unit isomorphism and not a
claim of crystalline or geometric origin. Inverting p IN the ring
modulo p² is not intended.

The comparison preserves the ACTUAL distinguished polynomial section:

    F(s)*(P(s^p),P'(s^p))^t=(P(s),P'(s))^t.            (15)

Indeed the vector on each side is the first column of the appropriate
G, and H_p e_1=e_1. The primes in(15) mean derivative in the polynomial's
own argument; the factor p*s^(p−1) belongs to the pullback connection
in(3), not to the coordinate vector in(15).

## 4. A finite rational representative modulo p² and legal half jets

No convergence of(6) is needed away from0. Define the FINITE polynomial

    R_p(s)=sum_(1≤j<2p, j odd, j≠p) s^j/j.             (16)

Every denominator is a p-unit. Partition the indices in(12) as
j=j_0+2pk. Their inverses satisfy 1/j=1/j_0 modulo p. It follows
coefficientwise that

    b_p(s)=p*R_p(s)/(1-s^(2p)) modulo p².               (17)

This retains the full range up to degree2p−1 and all geometric blocks;
no exponent is replaced by a field scalar. Inserting(17) into(11)
gives F_2∈Mat_2(C/p²), an explicit finite rational representative.
The expansion map C/p²→(Z_(p)/p²)[[s]] is injective because all
denominators have constant1. Therefore formal equality proves both
the rational horizontality identity(3) modulo p² and(14),(15) for
F_2. Equality of finite-precision formal series has not been used as
an unjustified evaluation of an infinite series at a unit.

The EXISTING endpoint data are R=Z_(p)[alpha]/(2alpha²−1), zeta=−alpha,
so zeta²=1/2. Both localization factors at zeta are units:

    1−zeta²=1/2,
    1−zeta^(2p)=1−2^(−p)=1/2 modulo p.                 (18)

Hence s→zeta+t defines a legitimate evaluation
`C/p²→(R/p²)[t]/(t²)`. It supplies literal values and first jets of
F_2 and the two pulled-back modules. All differentiated identities
are established in the ambient ring BEFORE this jet substitution;
d/dt is not claimed to preserve the ideal(t²).

This is still the explicitly chosen ambient lift s→s^p: its source
argument in the jet is `(zeta+t)^p`, not an unannounced linear
transport of t. It is NOT the etale coefficient automorphism
sigma(alpha)=−alpha on R. No endpoint relation is differentiated and

## 5. Why the unit initial normalization fails, exactly

For comparison, suppose the SAME horizontal problem had F_I(0)=I.
The rational integral gauge G transforms it to the unique
characteristic-zero formal solution

    H_I=[[1,ell(s)−ell(s^p)],[0,1]],
    F_I=G(s)H_I(s)G(s^p)^(-1).                         (19)

For every positive degree below p, the formal coefficients of ell
are p-integral. At degree p the top-right entry of H_I has coefficient

    1/p−1,                                            (20)

of valuation−1. This is the FIRST p-denominator. Multiplication by
the integral invertible gauges cannot remove its leading defect:
its coefficient residue is carried by

    G(0) N G(0)^(-1)=P(0)² N,

so the degree-p coefficient of (F_I)_(12) has residue P(0)²/p modulo
Z_(p), with P(0) a unit. No other nonintegral lower coefficient can
contribute at this first degree. Thus F_I is not integral.

There cannot instead be an unrelated integral solution of the
mod-p² equation with initial I that avoids this obstruction. Reduce
such a hypothetical solution modulo p. The p*s^(p−1) term vanishes,
so each column would be a horizontal solution of y'=A(s)y. Its
second scalar column y has y(0)=0, y'(0)=1 and obeys

    (j+2)(j+1)y_(j+2)
            =[j(j+1)−n(n+1)]y_j.                     (21)

For odd j=1,3,...,p−4 all denominators are units, and neither numerator
root n nor p−n−1=4m is odd. Thus y_(p−2) is a unit. At j=p−2 the
left side is0 whereas the right side is nonzero: its additional
factor equals 2−n(n+1)=20/9 modulo p, a unit for this prime family.
This is a contradiction. The p-scaled initial matrix in(3) is not
an arbitrary dismissal of a solvable unit normalization; it avoids
this explicit resonance by retaining one nonunit direction.

## 1. Actual source polynomial and all triangular denominators

Keep exactly the original primes `p congruent to 13 or 19 modulo 24`, `p=6m+1`, and `n=2m=(p-1)/3`. This n is not the earlier unrelated half-degree index. In this entire family n is even and `2n<p`. The previously reviewed quadratic paper, Section 3 (lines 97–140), identifies the exact finite `K_0` with normalized Legendre `P_n`, not a polynomial obtained by replacing integer exponents/parameters with field scalars. Hence P is even, has degree n, satisfies `P(1)=1` and the displayed L_n equation over characteristic zero. Its terminating coefficients have only p-unit denominators because all relevant factorial indices are below p and 2 is a unit. I checked that unchanged source passage and its prior pin rather than rerunning its proof.

On the odd subspace of degree at most `n-1`, the coefficient of `s^j` in `L_n U` is

`(j+2)(j+1)u_(j+2)+(n-j)(n+j+1)u_j`.

Equating this with `2(j+1)a_(j+1)` gives precisely recurrence (5), including the minus sign on its upper triangular term. Every diagonal factor is a nonzero positive integer: `1<=n-j<=n` and `n+j+1<=2n<p`. Thus descent starting at `u_(n+1)=0` proves existence and uniqueness within that odd polynomial space, with all u_j in Z_(p). The uniqueness is not a claim about arbitrary parity, higher-degree polynomials or formal solutions. No original-family prime exception is needed.

## 2. The frame, its inverse and the complete horizontal equation

Formal ell has derivative `q(s)=1/(1-s²)`. The product rule gives `L_n(P ell)=2P'`, so `Q=P ell-U` solves the same homogeneous equation. Its solution matrix factors as `G(I+ell N)`, with G and nilpotent N exactly as in (7). Consequently the Wronskian d satisfies `d'=2s d/(1-s²)`. Importantly,

`(1-s²)d=P²-(1-s²)P U'+(1-s²)P'U`

is a polynomial. It is constant and can legally be evaluated at 1, giving `P(1)²=1`. No value of the formal logarithm at 1 is taken. Thus `det G=(1-s²)^-1`; the adjugate gives the polynomial inverse (9). Direct column differentiation, using `L_n U=2P'`, also verifies `G'=AG-GN q(s)` with the stated sign.

At zero, parity makes G diagonal. Both diagonal entries lie in Z_(p) and their product is one, proving `P(0)` is a unit and `G(0)=diag(P(0),P(0)^-1)`. No endpoint scalar or possibly vanishing half-point quantity is divided out.

For H_p, the identities `NH_p=pN` and `H_pN=N` give

`H_p'=N q(s)H_p-p s^(p-1)H_p N q(s^p)`.

Differentiating `G(s)H_p G(s^p)^-1` and using the two frame identities cancels the nilpotent terms and leaves exactly

`F'=A(s)F-p s^(p-1)F A(s^p)`.

Both pullback terms and the chain factor are present. Since the diagonal G(0) commutes with `diag(1,p)`, the prescribed initial value is correct. The ordinary characteristic-zero linear matrix ODE gives a unique formal solution for the whole initial matrix. This is not uniqueness from a point value over a ring modulo p².

## 3. Integrality, finite precision and the actual section

At every odd exponent j divisible by p, the coefficients in `p ell(s)-ell(s^p)` cancel exactly: `p/j-1/(j/p)=0`. This includes all p-divisibility depths, not just degree p. At every other odd exponent the coefficient is `p/j` with a p-unit denominator. Therefore `b_p` lies in `p Z_(p)[[s]]` as a full formal series. Multiplication by the integral frames proves full formal integrality of F at zero.

The determinant calculation gives `p(1-s^(2p))/(1-s²)` exactly. This is p times a unit in the indicated localization/formal neighborhood. It is deliberately not an integral unit isomorphism. In characteristic-zero formal scalars it is invertible after inverting p; one must not attempt to invert p in the ring modulo p². The qualified isogeny-type description does not assert a crystalline/geometric origin or a canonical normalization.

The exact section identity (15) follows because `(P,P')^t` is G's first column and `H_p e_1=e_1`. Here `P'(s^p)` differentiates P in its own argument. The factor `p s^(p-1)` occurs in differentiating that pulled-back vector/connection, not in replacing its second coordinate. Thus this really preserves the distinguished actual P section, not an arbitrary fitted solution.

For finite precision, every positive odd j not divisible by p has a unique representation `j=j_0+2pk`, with `1<=j_0<2p`, j_0 odd and j_0 not p. Both denominators are units and

`p/j-p/j_0 = -2p²k/(j j_0)`.

This proves the full coefficientwise congruence (17), including all geometric blocks and the upper residues through `2p-1`. No field-scalar replacement of the exponent p or evaluation of an infinite logarithm is involved. The resulting F_2 is rational over C/p². Every inverted denominator has constant one, so expansion into formal series is injective even over this finite-precision ring. Therefore the formal identities imply rational horizontality, determinant and section identities for F_2. The exact characteristic-zero F itself is only asserted formally; this argument does not make it a rational function on all C or justify evaluating it at arbitrary arithmetic units.

## 4. Ordinary endpoint values and first jets are legal

In the existing endpoint ring, `zeta²=1/2` exactly. Hence `1-zeta²=1/2`, while `1-zeta^(2p)=1-2^-p` reduces to `1/2 modulo p`. Both are units. The assignment `s -> zeta+t` therefore defines the stated ring map from C/p² to `(R/p²)[t]/(t²)`. It gives F_2, its literal first jet and both module pullbacks without any convergence assumption for ell. The ambient differential identities are proved before substitution; D_t is not asserted to descend through `(t²)`.

The pulled-back argument is literally `(zeta+t)^p=zeta^p+p zeta^(p-1)t modulo t²`. Neither its value nor its tangent is silently replaced by an etale coefficient automorphism or an arbitrary t action. There is no claimed endpoint-ring endomorphism lifting this ambient coordinate map. In particular `P(zeta)=0` only modulo p, when that prior fact is used, is not a characteristic-zero vanishing statement. Nothing here needs to invert P(zeta) or infer a unit-point value of the formal F/ell. The finite rational representative, rather than the formal logarithm, supplies the legal endpoint data.

## 5. Both obstructions for initial matrix I are valid

The frame transforms initial I to initial I. Over characteristic zero the unique solution is `H_I=I+(ell(s)-ell(s^p))N`. All coefficients below degree p are p-integral. At degree p its upper-right coefficient is `1/p-1`. Since the frames and all lower coefficients are integral, the first nonintegral coefficient of F_I is carried by `G(0)NG(0)^-1=P(0)²N`. Thus its degree-p upper-right residue is `P(0)²/p modulo Z_(p)`, of valuation -1. This is equally an obstruction in the exact Q_p formal solution, not an artifact of a chosen finite truncation.
